Welcome to High Halden Church of England Primary School
On behalf of everyone at High Halden Church of England Primary School, I would like to warmly welcome you to our website. I hope it offers you a glimpse into the heart of our school — a caring, inclusive, and vibrant place where children are nurtured and inspired to flourish.
We are proud to be part of the Flourish Together Federation, a partnership between two small and unique Church of England schools: Woodchurch and High Halden. Together, we share a united vision of growth and flourishing, rooted in our shared Christian values. By working closely as a federation, we strengthen our communities, broaden opportunities for our pupils and staff, and celebrate the individuality of each school while benefiting from the strength of collaboration.
As a Church school, our Christian ethos underpins everything we do. Our values — generosity, respect, love, wisdom, trust, and hope — are more than words; they are guiding principles that shape our learning, our relationships, and our aspirations.
If you haven’t yet had the opportunity to visit our wonderful school, we would be delighted to show you around. Please don’t hesitate to get in touch — we look forward to welcoming you to our school family.
With warmest wishes,
Executive Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: High Halden Church of England Primary School - Grasshoppers
pageCache.text:
Grasshoppers
🦗 Welcome to Grasshoppers!
Hello and welcome to our Grasshoppers class page! 📚 We are a vibrant and energetic group made up of Year 3 and Year 4 pupils, where curiosity is encouraged and learning is an exciting adventure every day.
Our classroom is a place where children begin to take greater responsibility for their learning, develop resilience, and explore their creativity across a broad and engaging curriculum. We believe in nurturing confidence, kindness, and a growth mindset in all we do. 🌱
The Grasshoppers team is dedicated to supporting every child to reach their full potential, and we’re excited to share their journey with you. 🎨✏️
On this page (sections to the right), you’ll find helpful resources, class updates, and celebrations of our children’s wonderful achievements. Let’s hop into learning together! 💚
In Year 3 and 4, children begin the exciting journey into Key Stage 2, following a two-year rotating curriculum that allows them to explore subjects in greater depth and make wider connections across their learning. At this stage, there is a strong emphasis on developing mathematical fluency, particularly learning and securing times table facts, alongside improving reasoning and problem-solving skills. Reading and writing continue to be central, while opportunities are broadened through rich topic work, science investigations, and creative subjects. Children are also introduced to more formal lessons in modern foreign languages (French), laying the foundations for future language learning. This balance ensures pupils deepen their knowledge and skills while continuing to enjoy a wide range of engaging and enriching experiences. The overarching themes that guide our learning are outlined below, and we make links to them across the wider curriculum. Please also see the learning overviews and knowledge organisers (on the right) for more information about the knowledge and skills covered each term.

pageCache.pageTitle: High Halden Church of England Primary School - Inspection Reports
pageCache.text:
Inspection Reports
We're really proud of what both OFSTED and SIAMS had to say about our school!
🌟 In our most recent OFSTED report, inspectors described our school as “a harmonious community where pupils and adults work happily together.” There's a strong sense of pride throughout our school, and we’re especially pleased that the report recognised how “everybody is welcome.”
The school was praised for being ambitious in offering a rich and engaging curriculum — both inside and outside the classroom. Pupils even help shape what that learning looks like! 🧠📚 From trips to the city, beach, and museums to an ever-changing variety of after-school clubs, there’s always something exciting happening.
The report also highlighted how pupils rise to high expectations for behaviour, developing confidence and self-esteem in our safe and nurturing environment. 💫 Leadership opportunities — like House Captains and Worship Leaders — give children the chance to shine and take responsibility.
Parents, carers, and pupils alike have great confidence in how we handle concerns. Bullying is taken seriously, and any potential incidents are addressed quickly and thoroughly. In fact, many pupils said they’re not even aware of it happening! 💬🛡️
You can read the full OFSTED report below.
Meanwhile, our latest SIAMS inspection (Statutory Inspection of Anglican and Methodist Schools) recognised the strength of our school’s Christian vision, describing it as “deeply embedded” and central to everything we do. Rooted in a meaningful biblical narrative, our vision supports the strategic growth of the school and helps everyone grow together — children and adults alike. 🌱✨
The report highlighted the profound impact this vision and our shared values have on the wellbeing of the whole school community. There’s a strong sense of belonging here, and pupils are eager to contribute and support each other. ❤️
🌿 Creative learning — both indoors and outdoors — encourages a genuine love of learning across the school. While the idea of spirituality is developing, we’re continuing to work towards a clearer, shared understanding of how it can be explored and expressed by everyone.
🕯️ Collective worship was described as “engaging and relevant for all,” and it beautifully reflects our values and vision. We’re now looking to strengthen how we monitor and evaluate worship to make it even more impactful.
📖 In RE, pupils enjoy exploring big questions and taking part in creative learning opportunities that really spark interest. We're in the early stages of developing how we assess learning in RE and give children time to reflect on what it means to them personally.
Overall, we’re proud of the many strengths recognised in the report and excited about how we’ll continue growing as a nurturing, faith-filled school community.
You can read the full SIAMS report below.

pageCache.text:
PSHE & RSE
🌱 PSHE & RSE at High Halden C of E Primary School
“Education is about more than tests. It is about helping young people discover themselves.” – Anon
Our Intent
At High Halden Primary School, the intent of our PSHE (Personal, Social, Health and Economic Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) curriculum is simple but powerful: to keep children safe – both now and in the future.
Our curriculum is designed to give children the knowledge, skills, and attitudes they need to make positive, informed choices in potentially challenging or dangerous situations. We aim for every child to:
Understand risks, consequences, and the law
Build resilience, empathy, and a sense of responsibility for themselves and others
Become active thinkers and supportive bystanders in school and in the wider community
We believe that all children may face risks at some point in their lives, so all children deserve to know how to:
Keep themselves safe – both online and offline
Support and look out for one another
Seek help confidently when needed
📚 Our Curriculum
We use the Pol-Ed scheme of work to deliver a well-structured and engaging PSHE curriculum, fully aligned with the PSHE Association’s programme of study and the DfE statutory guidance for Health and Relationships Education.
Through carefully sequenced, age-appropriate teaching, children develop the ability to reflect, discuss, and apply what they learn to real-life situations.
Our PSHE & RSE curriculum centres around six core themes:
Relationships – Building healthy, respectful relationships and recognising unhealthy behaviours
Keeping Safe – Understanding personal safety, peer pressure, and online risks
Understanding the Law – Knowing the role of law in protecting people and the impact of choices
Wellbeing – Supporting mental and physical health, resilience, and emotional literacy
RSE – Understanding body changes, consent, respect, and safe relationships in an inclusive way
Transition – Preparing for changes, including moving to secondary school, with confidence and care
💬 Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
In EYFS, PSHE is taught daily through Personal, Social and Emotional Development (PSED). Children explore:
Relationships and feelings
Self-confidence and self-awareness
Empathy and restorative conflict resolution
Understanding appropriate behaviour
❤️ Relationships and Sex Education (RSE)
For the RSE element, we follow the Christopher Winter Project (CWP) – an evidence-based scheme that is inclusive, age-appropriate, and safe.
Building and maintaining healthy relationships
Understanding emotions, boundaries, and consent
Using correct terminology for body parts
Preparing for physical and emotional changes of puberty
Respect for self and others
Understanding different types of families and relationships
Parents are fully informed before RSE lessons. While Relationships Education is statutory, parents can request withdrawal from certain aspects of Sex Education, and we welcome open conversations about this.
British Values & Christian Values
Our PSHE curriculum is underpinned by the Fundamental British Values:
Democracy – Encouraging pupil voice and choice
Rule of Law – Understanding why rules exist and how they protect us
Individual Liberty – Supporting informed personal choices within safe boundaries
Mutual Respect – Valuing diversity and kindness
Tolerance – Respecting and including those with different faiths and beliefs
These are woven together with our Christian values of generosity, respect, love, trust, wisdom, and hope — fostering a culture of compassion, curiosity, and character.
🌟 Why PSHE & RSE Matter
PSHE & RSE are not just classroom subjects — they prepare our children to:
Be emotionally literate and socially responsible
Make safe, informed decisions
Respect others, regardless of differences
Thrive in an ever-changing world
Our provision is supported by the Life Skills Progression and Values in Action documents, which map out the skills and attributes we want every child to carry forward into life beyond High Halden.

pageCache.pageTitle: High Halden Church of England Primary School - Maths
pageCache.text:
Maths
➕ Mathematics at High Halden C of E Primary School
“The essence of mathematics is not to make simple things complicated, but to make complicated things simple.” — Stan Gudder
At High Halden, we believe that mathematics is a vital life skill. It helps children to think logically, solve problems, and approach challenges with confidence and curiosity. Our maths curriculum ensures that children do more than just learn numbers — they learn how to think like mathematicians.
We follow the White Rose Maths (WRM) scheme, underpinned by a Mastery Approach, which allows every child to build deep, sustainable understanding, step by step.
🌟 Our Vision for Maths
Maths is more than just numbers — it’s a language of logic, pattern, structure, and reasoning. At High Halden, we want every child to:
Develop confidence and fluency in number
Reason and explain using precise mathematical vocabulary
Apply their understanding to solve real-life and abstract problems
Feel enjoyment and a sense of achievement through challenge
We teach our pupils to understand, not memorise — giving them the tools to make connections and tackle new problems with resilience and creativity.
📚 Our Curriculum: Based on White Rose Maths
We follow the White Rose Maths scheme of learning from EYFS to Year 6. This provides a carefully sequenced, consistent and progressive approach to number, calculation, shape, measurement and statistics.
Each unit focuses on:
✅ Concrete – Pictorial – Abstract (CPA) approach ✅ Small steps that build deep understanding ✅ Fluency, reasoning and problem-solving woven into every lesson ✅ Daily practice and revisiting of key concepts
🔢 Calculation at High Halden
To support consistency and progression across the school, we follow the WRM Calculation Policy, which sets out the specific strategies, models and representations used in each year group.
Each operation is broken down into small, clear steps that allow children to master each method before moving on. Children are taught why methods work, not just how to do them.
📊 Key features of our approach to calculation:
Progression from concrete to pictorial to abstract representations
Consistent use of manipulatives (e.g. counters, base 10, place value charts)
Focus on mathematical vocabulary and explanation
Opportunities for reasoning, pattern spotting and generalising
Clear guidance for addition, subtraction, multiplication and division
Strong emphasis on number sense, place value and mental strategies
Each year group builds upon the last, ensuring a coherent journey from early number work in EYFS through to multi-step problems in upper Key Stage 2.
📄 You can view our full Calculation Policy below.
🧠 Maths Mastery: Our Approach in Action
Our teaching is rooted in the principles of Maths Mastery, which ensure all children:
Learn together at the same pace, with support and challenge built in
Focus on depth before breadth, exploring topics in detail
Use mathematical talk to explain and justify their thinking
See maths as something to be explored, not memorised
We use the Connective Model, which links structure, imagery, language, symbols and context — helping children fully grasp what they’re doing and why it works.
💡 How We Support All Learners
We believe every child can achieve in maths. To ensure success for all:
Concepts are broken into small, manageable steps
Children receive scaffolding and support where needed
There are regular opportunities for challenge, particularly for those working at greater depth
Pre-teaching and revisiting help address misconceptions and reinforce learning
Teachers use assessment for learning daily to adapt and respond to pupils' needs
✨ Making Maths Meaningful
We want children to see the relevance of maths in the real world. Across the curriculum and through enrichment opportunities, children explore how maths helps us:
Compare and analyse data
Solve problems in science and geography
Make sense of time, money, patterns and more
From maths trails and puzzle days to cross-curricular investigations, we give children opportunities to apply their learning in meaningful contexts.
👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Working in Partnership with Parents
We know that maths can sometimes feel intimidating — for children and adults alike! That’s why we:
Host parent workshops and provide calculation guides
Share vocabulary and methods so families can support learning at home
Use platforms like Class Dojo to celebrate maths successes and progress
Together, we nurture confident, capable mathematicians who are ready for the challenges of secondary school and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: High Halden Church of England Primary School - Music
pageCache.text:
Music
🎵 Music at High Halden C of E Primary School
“Music is a world within itself, with a language we all understand.” — Stevie Wonder
At High Halden, we believe music is for everyone. It inspires creativity, builds confidence, and connects us to cultures and communities across the world. Our music curriculum is designed to develop skills, ignite passion, and give children the tools to express themselves through sound.
Through listening, singing, playing, composing, evaluating and performing, our children experience music in many forms — from classical to contemporary, from local traditions to global genres. Where possible, we link music to other curriculum areas to add depth and meaning.
🎼 How We Teach Music
We follow the Charanga Music School programme of study, which aligns with the National Curriculum and is taught across the whole school. The scheme takes a spiral learning approach, meaning key skills and concepts are revisited regularly and explored in greater depth as children progress.
Each unit focuses on:
Listening & Appraising
Musical Activities (warm-ups, singing, playing tuned/untuned instruments, improvisation, composition)
This repetition-based approach ensures secure understanding and mastery of musical concepts.
🎹 Musical Instrument Progression
To give every child the opportunity to experience a variety of instruments, we follow a structured progression:
EYFS: Glockenspiels – exploring pitch, rhythm, and simple melodies
Year 1 & 2: Recorders – introducing musical notation and breath control
Year 3 & 4: Clarinets – taught with specialist support from the Kent Music Hub
Year 5 & 6: African Drums – developing rhythm, ensemble performance, and world music awareness
This progression ensures that by the end of Year 6, children have explored tuned, woodwind, and percussion instruments in a purposeful sequence.
🎤 Singing at High Halden
Singing is at the heart of our music curriculum.
Weekly singing assemblies build pitch, melody, and vocal control
Warm-up exercises and harmony work are taught explicitly
Children perform at school events, church services, and local community celebrations
Choir Club is open to children with a passion for singing and performing. One of the highlights of the year is representing our school at Young Voices, performing alongside thousands of other children at the O2 Arena in London.
🎼 Musician of the Month
Each month, we celebrate a Musician of the Month — exploring their life, style, and contribution to music. This exposes children to a diverse range of genres, cultures, and musical history, inspiring them to listen more widely and appreciate music from around the world.
🕊 Weekly Praise & Reflection
Our Music and RE Lead delivers a Weekly Praise & Reflection assembly, bringing together music, worship, and spirituality. This provides a meaningful moment for the whole school to sing, reflect, and celebrate together.
🎵 Peripatetic Music Lessons
In addition to whole-class music, we offer peripatetic lessons for individuals or small groups. These are taught by specialist tutors and can include a variety of instruments, giving children the chance to further develop their skills and passion for music.
💻 Technology and Creativity
Charanga’s digital tools enhance our music lessons, making learning inclusive and accessible for all. From composing online to exploring digital instruments, technology supports creativity in every lesson.
🌍 Beyond the Classroom
We believe music should be shared. Our children:
Take part in community performances
Join in special music days and cross-curricular projects
Experience live music and workshops from visiting musicians
Celebrate world music and cultures through an annual Languages and Music Day
🎯 Our Goals
By the end of Year 6, every child will have:
Experienced the full range of learning in the Model Music Curriculum
Played and performed using tuned, woodwind, and percussion instruments
Composed and recorded their own music
Developed confidence to perform for an audience
Gained an appreciation for a wide variety of musical genres and traditions
At High Halden, music is lively, inclusive and inspiring — giving every child the chance to find their voice.

pageCache.pageTitle: High Halden Church of England Primary School - Music Development
pageCache.text:
Music Development
At High Halden Church of England Primary School, music plays a vibrant role in school life. We believe every child should have the opportunity to enjoy, explore and succeed in music — whether that’s through the classroom curriculum, instrumental tuition, performances, or inspiring musical experiences.
This page outlines how we deliver music education across three key areas, and what we’re developing for the future.
📚 1. Curriculum Music
All pupils receive a high-quality, progressive music curriculum from Early Years to Year 6. Our curriculum is designed to:
🎵 Build musical knowledge and vocabulary
🥁 Develop practical skills through singing, rhythm, composing and instrument work
🎼 Introduce children to a wide range of musical genres, cultures and traditions
🧠 Foster creativity, expression, and confidence in performance
We follow the Model Music Curriculum (MMC) and enhance it with resources from Charanga. Lessons are delivered weekly and include a balance of listening, performing, and composing.
🎻 2. Instrumental Tuition & Ensembles
We offer small-group or individual music tuition for pupils who wish to learn an instrument. Currently, children can access lessons in:
🎹 Piano and keyboard
🥁 Drums and percussion
🎸 Guitar and ukulele
🎤 Singing and vocal coaching
These lessons are taught by visiting specialist tutors, and we work closely with the Kent Music Hub to support access and progression.
🎶 Extra-curricular Music Opportunities
🎤 Choir – open to KS2 pupils, performing regularly in and outside school
🎼 Instrumental groups – we are developing small ensembles for children learning instruments
🌟 Performance opportunities – including harvest, Christmas, and end-of-year concerts, class assemblies, and community events
🌍 3. Musical Experiences
We believe music education should be memorable and inspiring. Throughout the year, all pupils are involved in:
🎭 Musical productions and class performances
🎧 Live music workshops with visiting musicians and cultural groups
🎟️ Trips to concerts or music-themed experiences
💃 Links with dance, drama and RE to explore music in spiritual and cultural contexts
👩‍🎤 🎵 Musician of the Month
We are proud to take part in the Musician of the Month initiative — a brilliant way to promote musical appreciation and understanding across the whole school.
Each month, we focus on a new musician, composer or musical tradition, with music shared in assemblies, classrooms, and displays. This helps pupils:
🎧 Hear a wide range of live and recorded music
🌎 Discover artists from different genres, cultures and backgrounds
We highlight both well-known and emerging musicians, from Beethoven to Beyoncé, Ella Fitzgerald to Ed Sheeran — ensuring children experience a rich and diverse musical journey.
💬 Develop thoughtful responses to what they hear
💖 Learn to value music as a powerful form of expression
🌱 Future Plans for Music at High Halden
We are passionate about continually growing our music provision. Our current development goals include:
🎶 Expanding access to instrumental lessons for younger pupils
👩‍🏫 CPD for staff to enhance musical confidence and subject expertise
🏫 Increasing opportunities for live performance in the local community
🌐 Embedding digital music tools and apps into lessons
🧩 Strengthening cross-curricular links (e.g., music and literacy, history, or art)
📄 Our Full Music Development Plan
You can read more in our detailed plan: 📥 Download: HH_Music_Development_Plan.pdf

Our Governors
At the Flourish Together Federation, we are proud to have a single, dedicated Governing Body working across both High Halden CE Primary School and Woodchurch CE Primary School. Our governors bring together expertise, commitment, and perspectives from parents, staff, the church, the local authority, and the wider community.
Together, they ensure both schools flourish—providing the very best education, care, and opportunities for every child.
👩‍🏫 Who Are Our Governors?
Our Governing Body includes:
Parent Governors – elected by parents to represent families’ voices
Staff Governors – bringing professional insight from within school
Local Authority Governor – appointed by Kent County Council
Foundation Governors (Church) – ensuring our Christian ethos is upheld
Co-opted Governors – chosen for their skills and experience
Headteacher (Ex-officio) – contributing leadership and accountability
The Clerk to Governors supports the Governing Body by organising meetings, sharing documents, and keeping accurate records of discussions and decisions.
🎯 What Do Governors Do?
The Governing Body works at a strategic level to ensure the success of both schools within the Federation. Their responsibilities include:
✅ Ensuring Vision & Values – setting the Christian vision and ethos that guide our schools.
📊 Monitoring School Performance – holding leaders to account for pupil progress, teaching quality, and staff development.
💷 Overseeing School Finances – making sure budgets are well-managed and funding benefits all pupils.
📌 Policy & Planning – approving school policies and setting long-term priorities.
🧭 Community Insight – offering valuable perspectives and representing the views of our wider community.
🏫 How We Work
The full Governing Body meets once each term. Governors also:
Visit schools regularly to see teaching and learning in action
Take part in book looks, learning walks, and collective worship
Meet with subject leaders to discuss curriculum and progress
Attend training to strengthen governance skills
These activities ensure that policies and plans are not only written—but lived out daily in classrooms and across school life.

Remote Learning
At High Halden Church of England Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that our children continue to flourish, even when circumstances mean the school site cannot open as usual. Whether due to extreme weather, such as heavy snow, an emergency, or specific government instruction, we will immediately enact our Remote Learning Plan. As a proud Google School, we utilise Google Classroom and our suite of digital tools to provide high-quality, teacher-led learning from home. Our aim is to replicate the school timetable as closely as possible, ensuring children remain engaged with their curriculum, stay connected with their teachers, and continue to 'grow together' until we can safely return to the classroom. Specific instructions for accessing daily lessons will be shared via our standard communication channels at the earliest opportunity.

pageCache.pageTitle: High Halden Church of England Primary School - Science
pageCache.text:
Science
🔬 Science at High Halden C of E Primary School
“The important thing is to never stop questioning.” – Albert Einstein
At High Halden, we want every child to leave us with a scientist’s mindset — curious, questioning, and confident to explore the world around them.
Our Science curriculum is designed to:
Foster intrinsic curiosity about the universe
Encourage respect for both the living and non-living world
Equip pupils with the knowledge, concepts, skills, and attitudes to work scientifically and think critically
Science here is not just about facts — it’s about asking why, how, and what if. We nurture children to become independent thinkers, capable of planning and conducting investigations, using evidence to support their ideas, and communicating their findings with confidence.
🧪 Working Scientifically
We ensure that Working Scientifically skills are taught and built upon year by year. These skills are embedded in lessons so that pupils learn to:
Ask questions and develop lines of enquiry
Use equipment safely and accurately
Plan and carry out investigations
Analyse data and draw conclusions
Explain concepts clearly using scientific vocabulary
Our lessons incorporate a wide range of enquiry types:
⏳ Observation over time
📊 Classifying and grouping
⚖ Undertaking comparative and fair testing
📚 Research using secondary sources
At the heart of our teaching is first-hand experience — giving children practical, engaging opportunities to explore scientific ideas in real contexts.
🌱 Science Progression at High Halden
EYFS – Exploring the World
In the Early Years Foundation Stage, science is woven into Understanding the World. We spark curiosity by exploring:
Similarities and differences in objects and living things
Habitats and places in the local environment
Materials and their properties
Seasonal changes — especially within our own school grounds and the village of High Halden
These experiences lay the foundation for scientific thinking, encouraging children to ask questions, make observations, and talk about changes they notice.
Key Stage 1 (Years 1 & 2) – Building Foundations
Children begin to investigate the natural world more systematically, studying:
Animals (including humans) and their features
Senses and body parts
Everyday materials and their uses
Plants and their basic structures
They also learn about significant scientists who have changed the way we understand the world. Working in mixed-age classes allows pupils to revisit and deepen learning over a two-year cycle.
Lower Key Stage 2 (Years 3 & 4) – Expanding Knowledge
Pupils build on their KS1 learning by exploring:
Living things and their habitats
Plants (including functions and growth)
Ask their own scientific questions
Decide which type of enquiry will best answer them
Use scientific vocabulary in both discussion and writing
Draw simple conclusions from evidence
Upper Key Stage 2 (Years 5 & 6) – Deepening Understanding
By the end of primary school, pupils should have a broad and deep understanding of key scientific ideas. They study:
Living things and their life cycles
Animals, including humans (circulatory system, reproduction, health)
Properties and changes of materials
Evolution and inheritance
Advanced electricity and light
They explore more complex relationships and interactions, make systematic observations, and use data to justify their conclusions.
In Cycle A, they also investigate the work of British scientists and how their discoveries have shaped our world.
🌟 Our Science Vision
By the time they leave High Halden, our pupils will:
Think like scientists — questioning, reasoning, and testing ideas
Have a secure body of scientific knowledge ready for secondary school
Understand the importance of science in everyday life and the wider world
Appreciate the work of scientists past and present, and be inspired to see themselves as future innovators

Sports Premium
🏅 At High Halden Church of England Primary School, we believe in nurturing the whole child — body, mind, and spirit. 🌱 As part of our Christian ethos and school vision, we aim for all children to leave primary school physically literate, confident, and equipped with the skills, knowledge, and motivation to enjoy a lifelong love of sport and physical activity. ⚽🏃‍♀️🎾
🎯 What Is the Sports Premium?
The PE & Sports Premium is government funding provided to primary schools to help improve the quality of physical education, physical activity, and sport. The goal is to create self-sustaining, long-lasting impact that goes beyond the funding itself.
Raising the profile of PE and sport across the whole school 🏫
Increasing confidence, knowledge, and skills of all staff in teaching PE 🧑‍🏫
Expanding participation in a broader range of sports and activities 🏀🏓🏃‍♂️
Promoting active, healthy lifestyles 🌟
💪 Our Commitment
We use the Sports Premium to:
Deliver high-quality PE lessons across all year groups
Offer after-school sports clubs and competitive opportunities 🏆
Bring in qualified coaches to enhance children's learning
Improve and maintain equipment and resources for physical activity
Develop staff through specialist PE training
Through this, we ensure our pupils: ✔️ Gain confidence in their physical ability ✔️ Understand the importance of health and fitness ✔️ Embrace teamwork and sportsmanship ✔️ Access a wide range of inclusive sporting opportunities

Curriculum Organisation
At our school, we are proud to offer a carefully planned two-year rolling curriculum designed to meet the needs of our mixed-age classes from Year 1 to Year 6. This ensures that all pupils access the full breadth and depth of the National Curriculum, while allowing for thoughtful repetition, meaningful progression, and a rich variety of learning experiences.
To provide full coverage without overlap, our curriculum alternates between:
Cycle A – Academic Year 2025–2026
Cycle B – Academic Year 2026–2027
This structure supports our commitment to delivering a cohesive, well-sequenced curriculum, enabling children to build on prior knowledge and apply skills across a range of contexts. It also enhances opportunities for collaboration, peer learning, and cross-age dialogue, which are key strengths of our mixed-age model.
Alongside this, our Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum is designed in line with the statutory EYFS framework and is carefully sequenced to support children’s learning and development across all seven areas of learning. It is underpinned by a play-based approach that recognises the importance of active learning, exploration, and critical thinking, in line with the Characteristics of Effective Learning.
Our curriculum is responsive to the individual needs, interests, and developmental stages of each child, ensuring appropriate challenge and progression. While it reflects, where appropriate, whole-school themes, it is primarily shaped by ongoing observation and assessment of children’s interests, enabling practitioners to provide purposeful, engaging learning experiences. This approach ensures that all children develop the knowledge, skills, and attitudes they need for a strong start in their educational journey.
Together, our curriculum approach reflects our belief in inclusive, responsive teaching that meets every child where they are, and takes them further.

pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
🌿 Our School Vision
At High Halden Church of England Primary School, we take pride in creating a nurturing environment where every learner is loved, valued, and known as a unique individual. Rooted in God’s love, we provide rich experiences and a strong sense of belonging, enabling all children to grow, flourish, and bear fruit.
“I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit.” — John 15:5
✨ Our Curriculum Intent
With our Christian vision at the heart of all we do, we have worked closely with children, families, staff and the wider community to design a curriculum that reflects our rural setting, values and aspirations.
Our goal is to ensure that every child leaves High Halden equipped with the skills, knowledge, and character to succeed in life beyond our school gates.
We aim to nurture growth in three key areas:
🔎 Curiosity & Creativity
🎨 Enriching, first-hand experiences
💡 Inspirational, enquiry-led teaching
📚 A broad, active, and engaging curriculum
🏡 Strong Sense of Community
🌳 Learning rooted in our beautiful rural village
🤝 Working with local residents and community groups
🌍 Celebrating diversity and inclusion
🌟 Character Development
💪 Building resilience, confidence, and independence
🎯 Encouraging aspirations and a strong moral compass
✝️ Guided by our Christian values in all that we do
We also believe it is vital that children experience British culture and develop the ability to make informed choices in an ever-changing world. Our curriculum is designed to provide these opportunities in meaningful, age-appropriate ways.
📖 Reading, Writing & Mathematics
At High Halden, we prioritise literacy and numeracy as the foundations for all learning. We aim to ensure all children are:
📖 Literate – confident readers and communicators
➕ Numerate – secure and capable with numbers
These core skills open doors to future learning and opportunities.
🚀 Our Implementation
We believe that every child has a right to a great education — and that learning should be a joyful experience.
👩‍🏫 Teaching & Learning
🧠 Lessons are rich, fun, and meaningful
🎨 Teachers are encouraged to be creative and responsive
🗝️ Learning helps children make informed life choices
🌈 Teaching supports children to flourish in our wider community
🧩 Curriculum Design
We view children and teachers as co-creators of the curriculum. The High Halden Curriculum is:
🗺️ Tailored to our school’s unique context
🏞️ Reflective of our local environment and heritage
🎯 Focused on both depth and breadth, meeting all statutory requirements
🎣 Designed to hook, inspire and engage young minds
📚 Our Thematic Approach to Learning
At High Halden Primary School, we offer a curriculum that is rich, purposeful, and connected. Each term, we follow an overarching theme that links most subjects, helping children make meaningful connections in their learning.
These themes are usually driven by History or Geography, providing a strong foundation for pupils to explore the world around them — past and present — while inspiring curiosity, critical thinking and creativity.
